problem: Existing robot path planning is either human-agnostic or proximal human-aware. Neither handles remote robots in unfamiliar environments that must move in ways matching a teammate's intent. Instructors therefore often need extra clarification commands to fix the robot's position and orientation.
motivation: Effective human-robot teaming needs robots whose behavior meets human expectations even when they are out of sight. Fine-grained movement is needed to gather specific environment information through mapping and snapshots. Reducing clarification commands would make task completion more efficient and lower the burden on the instructor.
key_idea: Encode human intention from natural-dialogue navigation data, using known participant responses to executed commands to train a reinforcement learning policy for team-centric motion planning.
insight: Only the abstract is available and it reports no results or ablations. It frames team-centric planning as a distinct third area, alongside human-agnostic and proximal human-aware planning. Its central claim is that clarification commands in dialogue signal mismatch with instructor intention, and can serve as a training signal.
method: Data source: reuses methodology and data from an ongoing series of natural dialogue experiments in which naive participants instruct a remote robot in an unfamiliar environment.
Task setting: participants uncover specific environment information through real-time mapping and snapshots, which requires fine-grained robot movement.
Learning signal: known participant responses to executed commands are used as feedback to train an RL policy for building awareness about unknown environments.
Objective: maximize the relevant information relayed to the human instructor while minimizing instructor burden, in particular by reducing clarification commands.
